why: I compared the builder brief's test cases with the verifier's probes. Step 2 of the builder brief lists inputs with expected outputs that match the verifier's Check 1 probe almost exactly: "clamp(-5, 0, 100) === 0", "clamp(140, 0, 100) === 100", "clamp(50, 0, 100) === 50", "clamp(0, 0, 100) === 0", "clamp(100, 0, 100) === 100" and "clamp(7, 3, 3) === 3". Check 1 runs those same six cases and expects [0,100,50,0,100,3]. The brief also gives "clamp(5, 10, 0)" throwing a RangeError, which is the first case in Check 2's probe. Telling the builder to write its own tests is allowed. Handing it the verifier's own set of inputs and expected outputs is not, because it passes the checker's probe to the builder. Steps 1, 3 and 4 do no harm: step 4's npm test is named in an expect line, so it's allowed.
